transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Occupational health sent me down here. They... well, they think I'm not eating enough. 

I usually just stick to black coffee. Maybe a plain yogurt during the day. Sometimes a few bites of chicken at night, but that's about it. I just... eating a full meal, it feels like I'm letting my standards slip. I don't really see the issue, but they told me I had to come in.
Do you have a fear of gaining weight or feel like you need to restrict your food intake to manage your weight or shape?

I don't know if I'd call it fear. It's just... discipline. 

But... if the scale is up, even by half a pound, I get this... jolt, I guess. Like things are slipping out of my control. So, yeah, if that happens, I'll spend the day cutting back harder. I just can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. That's all it is.
When you're trying to control your weight or shape, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively?

No. I don't do any of that. 

I just... keep my eating in check. I don't make myself sick or take pills or anything like that. And I'm not spending hours at a gym. I just stick to my routine.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms or health issues because of your eating habits, like feeling lightheaded, having trouble concentrating, or changes in your menstrual cycle?

I haven't really noticed any of that. I do my job just fine. 

The nurse at occupational health made a big deal about my weight, though. She said it was... dangerously low. I mean, I guess my uniform hangs off me a bit now. I've had to tighten my duty belt past the old notches. But... I don't know. When she told me the number, I still just thought... I could stand to be a little sharper. 

I don't feel sick, if that's what you're asking.
Do you feel that you are overweight or do you have a strong desire to be thinner, even though others may tell you that you are underweight?

I don't know about "overweight." I just... I don't see what everyone else claims they see. 

When I look in the mirror, I'm just looking at my stomach. My waist. If it's not... lean enough, it just ruins the day. I can't respect myself if I let it get soft. So, yeah, I guess I want to be thinner. Or just... tighter. I don't really care what other people think is underweight.
Can you tell me what your current weight is, and whether a healthcare professional has ever told you that it is below a healthy range?

I don't... I don't really know the exact number right now. I don't step on the scale much anymore. 

Like I said, the nurse at work mentioned something about it being too low. But... I don't really pay attention to the specific numbers.
When you restrict your food, is it primarily because you fear gaining weight, or is it more about feeling like you've lost control if your body isn't how you want it to be?

I guess... it's a bit of both. 

If I see the scale go up... even just half a pound... I get this sort of... jolt. Like things are slipping away from me. 

If that happens, I just... I cut back more that day. I just can't stand the thought of putting it back on.
Can you tell me approximately how tall you are, and if you know, what your Body Mass Index (BMI) might be based on your height and weight?
I'm about five foot ten. As for the other thing... the BMI... I don't know. I don't calculate that sort of thing. I just focus on how I look.
Based on your height of five foot ten and the nurse's concern about your weight being dangerously low, would you say your Body Mass Index (BMI) is below 18.5?

I suppose it must be. I don't track the exact math... but my uniform hangs off me now. I've had to... tighten my belt past the old notches. 

Even when the nurse said it was dangerously low, I just... I still thought I could stand to be a little sharper.
When you look in the mirror and see your body, does it match how you feel about yourself, or do you see a version of yourself that feels inaccurate or distorted?

I don't know about... distorted. I just don't see what everyone else keeps saying they see. 

I mostly just look at my stomach. My waist. If I don't look lean enough in the mirror... I can't really respect myself. It pretty much decides how my whole day is going to go.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition or another mental health disorder that could explain your desire to be thinner or your restrictive eating habits?
No. I haven't been diagnosed with anything else. Just... regular check-ups for work, and I've always passed those fine. There's no other condition.
When you restrict your eating, is it mostly because you believe you need to change how your body looks, or would you say you're doing it for other reasons, like health or discipline?
I don't really know. I haven't... spent much time analyzing it in those terms. It's just how I've been doing things.
Would you say your restrictive eating is more about controlling your weight, or more about how you perceive your body shape?
I'm not really sure. I don't see much of a difference between the two, to be honest. It's just... about keeping the gut off. I don't overthink it beyond that.
Would you say that your overall sense of self-worth depends strongly on your body weight or shape?

I guess... yeah. It does. I mean, when I look in the mirror, I don't see what other people claim they see. I just... I look at my stomach. My waist. If I don't look lean enough, it just ruins the day. I can't really respect myself if I let that go. That's just how it is.
